lines.native: I'm Marginalia. Questa è la storia di Journathan, l'uomo dalle molte lingue. Il suo viaggio verso casa dura vent'anni. This is The Journey. I sell books only to people who understand them. A controversial business model. Dove va Journathan?
lines.translation: I'm Marginalia. This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years. This is The Journey. I sell books only to people who understand them. A controversial business model. Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: A bookworm peers from a half-eaten dictionary. The remaining half has been corrected in red ink.

lines.native: Un libro è una cosa. La domanda è: dove va Journathan? You have identified the merchandise, not his destination. Reading comprehension: pending. Rileggi: «Il suo viaggio verso casa dura vent'anni.» Dove va Journathan?
lines.translation: A book is a thing. The question is: where is Journathan going? You have identified the merchandise, not his destination. Reading comprehension: pending. Read again: “His journey home lasts twenty years.” Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small question mark beside you. The pencil appears accustomed to disappointment.

lines.native: Hai capito, ma la risposta è in inglese. The destination is correct; the language is not. Reading comprehension: promising, footnote required. Dove va Journathan? Rispondi in italiano.
lines.translation: You understood, but the answer is in English. The destination is correct; the language is not. Reading comprehension: promising, footnote required. Where is Journathan going? Answer in Italian.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small question mark beside your elbow. Apparently, you are now a revised edition.

lines.native: Esatto, va a casa! Reading comprehension: redeemed. Ora leggo: Il Ciclope chiede il suo nome. Journathan risponde: «Il mio nome è Nessuno.» The first recorded translation trick. No spoilers; the Cyclops had a difficult reading experience. Quale nome dà Journathan al Ciclope?
lines.translation: Exactly, he goes home! Reading comprehension: redeemed. Now I read: The Cyclops asks his name. Journathan replies: “My name is Nobody.” The first recorded translation trick. No spoilers; the Cyclops had a difficult reading experience. What name does Journathan give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a tick beside your sleeve, then opens a book whose margins have survived only through negotiation.

lines.native: Journathan è il suo vero nome. Ma quale nome dà al Ciclope? The real name: correct. The reading comprehension: not yet. Rileggo: Il Ciclope chiede il suo nome. Journathan risponde: «Il mio nome è Nessuno.» Quale nome dà Journathan al Ciclope?
lines.translation: Journathan is his real name. But what name does he give the Cyclops? The real name: correct. The reading comprehension: not yet. I’ll read it again: The Cyclops asks his name. Journathan replies: “My name is Nobody.” What name does Journathan give the Cyclops?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently customers come with margins.

lines.native: Esatto! Il suo nome è Journathan, ma al Ciclope dà il nome «Nessuno». Hai capito il testo. Il libro è tuo. Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the missing pages were lunch.
lines.translation: Correct! His name is Journathan, but he gives the Cyclops the name “Nobody.” You understood the text. The book is yours. Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the missing pages were lunch.
lines.narrative: Marginalia stamps the receipt in the margin, where she considers all important business belongs. The book bears only a few bite marks.
